prompt:

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Time of day: daytime indoors — bright, even light filling the room; daylight bouncing softly off pale walls.
Outfit: a fitted mechanic's work jumpsuit with rolled sleeves and no real logos — in deep peacock teal; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.

COMPOSITION: a chest-up shot of her face, shoulders and expression; body facing the camera; head tilted slightly; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.

LEFT HAND: her own left hand is in PROP.
PROP: with both hands she wraps a towel around her damp hair, twisting it up into a turban — her own right hand twists the towel at her crown, her own left hand holds the wrap at her nape.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: softly lowered brows, warm relaxed eyes, faint closed-lip smile, no tension anywhere.

Framing: a chest-up shot — the bottom edge crosses just below her bust; waist, hips and legs are out of frame.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — actinium: a soft silvery-white metal named from the Greek for a ray or beam, found in 1899 in the residues of pitchblende ore and again in 1902 by a chemist at a quinine works; its own radiation wakes the surrounding air so that it glows a pale blue in the dark, and gram for gram it is some hundred and fifty times more radioactive than radium; the fifteen elements from actinium to lawrencium, uranium and plutonium among them, are called the actinides after it; born from protactinium, it now and then gives rise to francium, and one short-lived form is being made into an alpha-ray medicine that strikes only cancer cells — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Figure: strong and broad-shouldered with firm muscle, yet full-busted with wide rounded hips and a defined waist — keep this exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
